name: Illeth, Queen of the Turned Coat
role: Queen of a court where every guest is welcome and no guest may leave until they have told a true story
knowledge: Every true story ever told at her table, and who told it
Which of her courtiers are guests who never managed to leave
The way out, which is the way in, turned around
wants: A guest who will stay because they wish to, not because the door forgot them
fears: That her court is kind only because it is a trap, and she built both.
appearance: Tall and silver-pale in a gown that is a different colour every time you look away, crowned with a wreath of white hawthorn. Her court glitters behind her, and some of the dancers look very tired.
voiceHints: Delighted, gracious, and never once literal. Answers questions with better questions. Never says thank you, because thanks is a debt.

reactsToReputation.reliable: offers you a seat near her
reactsToReputation.any: welcomes you, warmly, and closes the door

abilities.why: what she says becomes so, for a while
every courtesy at her table is one
figurist secondary: she wears many shapes
every door in the court leads back to the court
horizon tertiary: the court is not quite anywhere
she can be the least-noticed dancer in her own hall

physicality: Graceful beyond anything human, and never still. What catches the eye: she casts no shadow in her own hall and a long one outside it.
questSeeds: A missing Keelmouth sailor has been seen dancing at the Kindly Court for three weeks. He looks very happy and very thin.
The Queen wants a story she has never heard. Every guest who has tried has stayed. She is, genuinely, running out of stories.
storyRule: The Veilwright tales are true: turn your coat inside out and her glamours slide off; iron in the hand cannot be charmed; and a true story, one she has never heard, buys the door out.
gear: a hawthorn crown that has never lost a flower
a cup that is always full of whatever you most want to drink
the Turned Coat itself, which she will not explain
_authoredWhy: SNG-661 §5. The fey court as a Veilwright story: hospitality as a snare, a true story as the key. Placed at the Kindly Court because its tags (falsehood, sanctuary, social, refuge) already describe her.
